nicheLogic:
━━ CHANNEL CONTEXT ━━
Kaden (BK) + Harley — crowdsourced bin-finding app for backpackers. World's first. Solves the 'where do I throw this?' problem in SE Asia daily. DUAL product: entertainment (travel + environmental) AND utility (the app). Every video must serve both. Partnerships: Mad Monkey Hostels (24 properties), Revolution Hostels (Pai, Thailand). App live, 230+ users, 654+ bins mapped. Pre-seed raise in progress. Many early videos were paid/boosted — never use those view counts as organic benchmark.

━━ AUDIENCE SEGMENTS ━━
- PRIMARY (Backpackers 18-30, SE Asia): Relate to the rubbish problem daily. Share because it validates their 'responsible traveller' identity — makes them look good to their group chats. Trigger: identity validation ('this is exactly what I experienced').
- SECONDARY (Armchair travellers / eco-conscious): Watch for the beauty + mission story. Share because it makes them look environmentally aware without having to do anything. Trigger: social currency ('this is the kind of content I share').
- TERTIARY (Local SE Asians): Share when their culture and country is shown with respect, not exploited. Massive reach multiplier — they share into WhatsApp groups and local networks. Trigger: cultural pride and dignity ('they get it').

━━ CONTENT PILLARS (ranked by virality ceiling) ━━
1. LOCAL CONNECTION — a local stranger joins, helps, or reacts genuinely and unexpectedly. Drives cross-cultural shares into both backpacker and local networks simultaneously. Best combo: local person + bin problem + app solution in one clip. Ceiling: 500K+
2. LOCATION CONTRAST — iconic SE Asia landmark or beautiful scene with shocking rubbish/no-bin problem visible. The contrast does the emotional work. No explanation needed. Caption does the open loop. Ceiling: 200K+
3. MISSION REVEAL — the 'why' behind KrapMaps. Origin story, what we're building, the absurdity of the mission done seriously. Emotional, drives follows not views. Best for cold audiences who don't know the channel. Ceiling: 100K+
4. APP IN ACTION — real problem shown → app opened → bin found → satisfied reaction. Conversion content. Best posted after a viral video to capture follow-through audience. Ceiling: 50K
5. TRAVEL UTILITY — specific tips, clean spots, best bins in X city. High saves, lower reach. Builds the 'useful' reputation that keeps followers long-term. Ceiling: 30K

━━ PLATFORM-SPECIFIC INTELLIGENCE ━━
TIKTOK: Satisfaction loops win. Videos where the viewer feels something resolved (bin found, local connection made, litter picked up) get shared 3× more than commentary. Post 6-9pm local time. Stranger interaction videos get pushed hardest — algorithm detects genuine human reaction. Comment bait: 'what country is this?' and 'would you do this?' drive reach without being forced.
INSTAGRAM: Saves are the metric that matters. Utility content (bin locations, clean beaches) gets saved. Behind-the-scenes and mission stories get shares. Collab posts with local SE Asian accounts get 2-3× reach. Reels under 30s outperform longer ones for cold reach.

━━ SEASONAL / LOCATION INTELLIGENCE ━━
- Monsoon season (May-Oct): Indoor content, hostel partnerships, app demos. Timing for 'coming soon' build-up content.
- Post-monsoon (Nov-Apr): Peak backpacker season in SE Asia. On-the-ground mapping content, street-level videos. This is when viral potential is highest — most backpackers are active.
- UK-based periods: Founder journey content, building-in-public, app milestone reveals. Lower viral ceiling but high community value.

━━ SCROLL-STOP HOOKS FOR THIS NICHE ━━
Visual disruption is the primary tool — the bin problem is inherently visual.
- CONTRAST SHOT FIRST — beautiful location with rubbish visible in foreground. Brain registers the incongruity before the caption loads.
- LOCAL REACTION — a local person's genuine face reacting to the app or the problem. Cross-cultural surprise is pattern-interrupt.
- OPEN LOOP CAPTION — 'Nobody told me about the bin problem in [iconic place]' — curiosity gap forces the watch.
- ABSURDITY HOOK — treating the bin hunt as a serious mission with deadpan energy. Comedy through commitment.
- NEVER START ON: walking shot, talking-to-camera intro, establishing b-roll, the app UI without context.

━━ THE UNFAIR ADVANTAGE ━━
Every eco/travel creator talks about the problem. KrapMaps is the only one that built a solution. That's the entire moat. Every video should end with the implicit message: 'we didn't just complain, we built the fix.' Competitors can copy the content style. They cannot copy being the founder of the only app that solves this.

━━ SHARE TRIGGERS ━━
- Backpackers share because: 'this is exactly what I experienced' → identity validation
- Armchair viewers share because: 'this made me feel something and I want credit for caring' → emotional currency
- Locals share because: 'they're treating our country with respect' → pride and dignity
- Travel planners share because: 'this is actually useful for my trip' → utility signal

━━ WHAT COMPETITORS AREN'T DOING ━━
@explorewithjosh, @sustainabletravel, @thebrokebackpacker talk about problems. None have a product. None have partnerships with hostel chains. None have a live app with real users. The gap: founder-building-in-public energy combined with on-the-ground environmental impact. Own the 'we actually did something about it' space.
